clue.text: Ralph got to marry the captain's daughter and torture a cabinet minister

definitions.text: Ralph got to marry the captain's daughter

parts.note: the rack is an instrument of torture, and to rack is to torture
Jack Straw was a Labour cabinet minister (Home and then Foreign Secretary) when the puzzle appeared

explanation.surface: A man called Ralph weds his captain's daughter and then tortures a government minister.
explanation.walkthrough: Ralph Rackstraw is the sailor in Gilbert and Sullivan's HMS Pinafore who wins Josephine, the captain's daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gilbert and Sullivan seaman who ends up marrying Captain Corcoran's daughter Josephine is surnamed thus.

clue.text: Values a means of revenue

definitions.meaning: to value something is to rate it
local property taxes in Britain were long called the ..., a source of council income

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: estimates of worth, and the British local property tax that funded councils.

clue.text: Board for 18 and vet, they say

definitions.note: 18 is KING'S PAWN, a chess piece, played on a chequered board

indicators.note: what people say is heard rather than read, so a sound-alike is wanted

parts.note: one who vets or examines something is a checker

explanation.surface: Looking for a board to play on and also a veterinary surgeon, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 across is a chessman, so the board meant is the chessboard; a chequer is the chessboard pattern, and an old word for such a board.
explanation.definitionFit: A chequer is a checked board of the kind chess pieces stand on, as in the old exchequer counting board.

clue.text: Talk of (but not at) work

parts.note: talking about your job away from it is a set phrase built on a word meaning workplace, which here is not where you are

explanation.surface: Chatter about the job, though not while actually on the job.
explanation.walkthrough: The parenthesis plays on the two senses: the word follows 'talk' in the idiom for discussing work, yet also names a workplace, which the talker is not in.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk shop is to discuss your work socially, and a shop is also a workplace.

clue.text: Libertine or collector

definitions.meaning: a dissolute pleasure-seeking man, a roué
a garden tool that gathers leaves together

explanation.definitionFit: A rake is both a debauched man about town and the toothed tool that gathers up leaves.

clue.text: Scene of 12 giving the first part of 14 across an end

indicators.note: something that gives is pliable and yields, so these letters bend into a new order

parts.note: 14 across is WORLD SOUL, whose first word is world
taken as written

explanation.surface: The setting of the stories is found by treating the start of another entry and finishing it off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving' is the anagram signal: WORLD plus AN END is rearranged. 12 down is ADVENTURES, as in Alice's Adventures in Wonderland.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis Carroll's Alice has her Adventures in Wonderland, so it is the setting of those adventures.

clue.text: Ungrammatical vermin in 5

definitions.meaning: 'a lice' pairs a singular article with a plural noun, which is bad grammar
5 down is WONDERLAND, home of Carroll's heroine

explanation.definitionFit: Carroll's heroine is the girl in Wonderland, and her name splits into an ungrammatical 'a lice'.

clue.text: To enlarge silver and a bit of gold currency is ecstasy

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: only a small bit of the word gold is taken, its first letter

parts.note: the rand is South Africa's currency
taken as written
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Investing in silver and gold coin is a thrilling way to grow rich.
explanation.definitionFit: To aggrandise is to make greater in power, wealth or size, a synonym of enlarge.

clue.text: Setting of 3 or 6 across after 3's conversion — I take grass

definitions.text: Setting of 3 or 6 across after 3's conversion
definitions.note: 3 is SHOP and 6 across is ALICE; in Through the Looking-Glass the sheep's shop turns into a rowing boat with Alice in it

parts.note: to nab is to take or seize
oat is a cereal grass

explanation.surface: A note about where a shop or a girl ends up once the shop is transformed, plus a confession about seizing grass.
explanation.walkthrough: In the 'Wool and Water' chapter of Through the Looking-Glass the Sheep's shop changes into a boat, so Alice, and the shop, end up in a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: After the shop is converted in Carroll's sequel, the girl and the knitting Sheep find themselves rowing on water.

clue.text: Essex man's instrument's piercing tone's a problem

indicators.note: one piece pierces the other, so it sits inside it
the letters are a problem to be worked out, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, with its s
the sax, short for saxophone, is a musical instrument

explanation.surface: A man from Essex complains that his saxophone's shrill note is causing trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'problem' makes EASTON, and 'piercing' sets the instrument inside. The East Saxons founded the kingdom whose name became Essex, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Essex takes its name from the East Saxons, so an early inhabitant of the kingdom was one of them.

clue.text: See 17
See 13
Favourite (singular 6 across unfinished) flowers typically are

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

indicators.note: the phrase lacks its final letter

parts.note: 6 across read as 'a lice' becomes, in the singular, 'a louse'

explanation.surface: A favourite girl, unfinished business, and a remark on what flowers are like.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 across is ALICE, taken as A LICE; made singular it is A LOUSE, and 'unfinished' drops its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Petalous means having petals, which is what flowers usually have.

clue.text: What were the chances of 5 in a set?

definitions.text: What were the chances of 5 in a set?

parts.words: What were the chances of 5 in a set?
parts.note: the risky escapades in 5 down, Wonderland, form the title of Carroll's book, read as a question about odds

explanation.surface: A question about the odds of finding Wonderland among a collection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chances' looks like odds, but it means hazardous happenings, the title word of Alice's Adventures in Wonderland.
explanation.definitionFit: Adventures are risky ventures or chance happenings, and Carroll's book is Alice's Adventures in Wonderland.

clue.text: Dove like this in replica, beautiful stuff in 5

definitions.text: Dove like this in replica, beautiful stuff in 5

parts.note: mock means imitation or replica, as in mock Tudor
a turtle dove is a dove of this kind
in Wonderland the Mock Turtle sings 'Beautiful Soup'

explanation.surface: A kind of dove copied, and a lovely substance found in Wonderland.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mock Turtle in Wonderland is named after the imitation turtle soup made from calf's head, and sings 'Beautiful Soup'.
explanation.definitionFit: Imitation turtle soup, made with calf's head, is the dish that gave Carroll's Mock Turtle its name.

clue.text: Platonic or Hegelian concept would nearly encompass maverick lords

indicators.note: one piece goes round the other
the word is not quite complete, losing its last letter

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

indicators.note: a maverick is unorthodox and wayward, so the letters stray into a new order

explanation.surface: A philosopher's idea that would almost surround a band of rebellious peers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' drops the last letter, 'maverick' gives RLDSO, and 'encompass' wraps the trimmed word round it. Hegel's world spirit and Plato's anima mundi are the concepts meant.
explanation.definitionFit: The world soul, anima mundi, is the idea of a soul animating the whole universe, found in Plato and in Hegel.

clue.text: What is the result of speeding?

definitions.text: What is the result of speeding?

parts.words: What is the result of speeding?
parts.note: reads like a question about fines and penalties, but asks how a hurried action is done

explanation.surface: A driver wonders what happens if caught going too fast.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a speeding ticket; the answer simply describes doing anything quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done at speed is done hurriedly, which is the adverbial phrase here.

clue.text: Boy turns to beast when fighting addiction

indicators.note: the boy's name turns round to run backwards

parts.note: Ted is a boy's name
an ox is a beast of burden

explanation.surface: A lad transforms into an animal while battling his habit.
explanation.definitionFit: Detox, short for detoxification, is treatment for getting off drink or drugs, i.e. fighting an addiction.

clue.text: Press baron?

parts.note: a newspaper owner given a peerage, but also baron read as a rank, which a newspaper calls one of these

explanation.surface: A newspaper magnate.
explanation.walkthrough: A baron in the press is a peer, but 'baron' is itself a rank, and a newspaper also has its own name.
explanation.definitionFit: Baron is a title of nobility, and a press, a newspaper, has a title on its masthead.

clue.text: Where 6 across went from time to time, should he (John, the boss) want a good girl

parts.note: 'from Monday to Friday' is 'Monday through Friday', so 'from ... to' gives this word
taken as written
a john is slang for a lavatory, as is loo
the king is the one in charge
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: Alice went somewhere now and then, and her journey depends on whether the boss wants a nice girl.
explanation.walkthrough: Alice went through the mirror in Carroll's sequel. 'from time to' is the American 'through' of time spans; LOO is British slang for a lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: In Carroll's sequel 6 across, Alice, climbs through the mirror above the mantelpiece into the reflected world.

clue.text: A chessman or three like good eggs

definitions.meaning: the pawn standing in front of the king at the start of a chess game
'king' as in king prawn means top quality, and spawn means fish eggs

explanation.definitionFit: The pawn in front of the king is a chess piece, and the letters regroup into spawn fit for a king.

clue.text: Ox of history or ox of oratory?

indicators.note: oratory is speech, so the words are as spoken

parts.note: taken as written, the two words of the clue said together

explanation.surface: Asking whether an ancient ox or a speaking ox is meant.
explanation.walkthrough: The aurochs is the extinct wild ox; said aloud it sounds like the clue's own words 'or ox'.
explanation.definitionFit: The aurochs was the wild ox of Europe, extinct since 1627, so it belongs to history.

clue.text: Man at bridge wants Hearts or a different suit

parts.note: H is the card-game abbreviation for hearts
taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: the letters are made different by being rearranged

explanation.surface: A card player at the bridge table wants hearts or another suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridge' suggests the card game, but it is the bridge Horatius held against the Etruscans in Roman legend.
explanation.definitionFit: Horatius Cocles is the Roman who defended the Sublician bridge, as in Macaulay's poem.

clue.text: Footman in 5 — croquet, reportedly?

definitions.meaning: the ...-Footman opens the Duchess's door in Wonderland
croquet said aloud suggests 'croak', the noise this creature makes

explanation.definitionFit: A frog serves as a footman in Wonderland, and frogs croak, which croquet resembles in speech.

clue.text: Found in morgues, some who were shot

indicators.note: the letters are found inside the run of words

explanation.surface: Bodies found in mortuaries, some of them victims of shooting.
explanation.walkthrough: The morgue picture makes 'shot' look like a gunshot victim, but it is a shot in the sense of an attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot, as in a shot in the dark, is an attempt at an answer, so a guess.

clue.text: Maker of priestly garments?

parts.note: the tribe of Israel's priests shares its name with ... Strauss, maker of denim jeans

explanation.surface: Who makes clothes for clergy?
explanation.walkthrough: Levi was the priestly tribe of Israel, and Levi Strauss made jeans, so his garments are playfully 'priestly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Levi Strauss founded the jeans company, and Levi is the tribe from which Israel's priests came.

clue.text: Footman in 5, said to be somewhat officious

indicators.note: the words are as said, not as written

parts.note: part of the word officious, the stretch spelt with ffici in the middle, is pronounced like the name of a swimming creature

explanation.surface: A servant in Wonderland who is a bit bossy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fish-Footman delivers the Queen's croquet invitation in Wonderland; the middle of 'officious' is pronounced with this sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Carroll's Fish-Footman brings the Duchess an invitation from the Queen in Wonderland.

clue.text: 2 articles hardly do what can't be done

indicators.note: hardly here means harshly, roughly, so the letters are roughly handled

parts.note: 2 down is chequer

explanation.surface: Two newspaper pieces could scarcely achieve the impossible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hardly' is the anagram signal, rearranging CHEQUER (2 down) with ARTICLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Squaring the circle was proved impossible, so it is the idiom for attempting what cannot be done.

clue.text: Disposition of doublet, hose, etc

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: The character of Elizabethan clothing, doublet and hose and the like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'etc' simply rounds off the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethos is the characteristic spirit or disposition of a person or community.

clue.text: He spies it out by addition of letters

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A spy picks something out by adding up letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges HE SPIES IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Epithesis is a linguistic term for adding a letter or sound to the end of a word.
